This site accompanies the *Tal om Kvinnor* project at Lund University.
It reports how the Swedish Riksdag spoke about women between 1900 and
1940, using the openly published
[Swedish Parliament Corpus](https://github.com/swerik-project/the-swedish-parliament-corpus)
as its raw material.

Each page presents one slice of that story. **Baselines** report raw
utterance and word counts; **Relative word frequencies** report each
category's share of the total. Every headline view is available for the
whole period and for either chamber separately.

## Terminology

Three keyword categories are used throughout the site:

- **kvinna 1** — a single broad wildcard `kvinn*` that matches any word
  starting with *kvinn*.
- **Kvinna 2** — a hand-picked list of generic feminine terms, pronouns
  and kin relations (`dam`, `dotter*`, `flick*`, `mor`, ...).
- **Kvinna 3** — a large list of specific and often work-related female
  titles (`barnmorska`, `hushållerska`, `piga*`, ...).

The categories are guaranteed pairwise disjoint by an automated check;
where a name appears in more than one list a Kvinna 2 entry always wins
over Kvinna 3. Older pages sometimes show a **kvinna all** line — that
is the union of all three, i.e. any utterance/word matching at least
one category. It sits above the individual category lines by
construction.


## Corpus figures

```{python}
from tok_preparer.src.data import read_word_frequencies
import tok_plots
import pandas as pd

df = read_word_frequencies()
df = df.copy()
df["gender"] = df["gender"].fillna("unknown")
tok_plots.configure()
```

The three heatmaps below split the corpus by chamber and by the
speaker's recorded gender, and count both **utterances** and **words**.
The first heatmap covers everything before 1920; the second covers the
whole 1900–1940 window; the third covers 1920 onwards. The two blocks
of years bracket the introduction of women's suffrage in 1919, which
lets us see how the gendered composition of the recorded discourse
shifts once women can vote.

```{python}
from IPython.display import Markdown, display

GENDERS = ["man", "woman", "unknown"]
CHAMBERS = [1, 2]
COLUMNS = ["utterance_count", "total_words"]
COLUMN_LABELS = {"utterance_count": "utterances", "total_words": "words"}


def cell_labels():
    return [f"Chamber {c} · {g}" for c in CHAMBERS for g in GENDERS]


def summary_frame(subset):
    grouped = subset.groupby(["chamber", "gender"], as_index=False)[COLUMNS].sum()
    values = {col: [] for col in COLUMNS}
    for c in CHAMBERS:
        for g in GENDERS:
            row = grouped[(grouped.chamber == c) & (grouped.gender == g)]
            for col in COLUMNS:
                values[col].append(int(row[col].iloc[0]) if not row.empty else 0)
    return pd.DataFrame(
        {"metric": [COLUMN_LABELS[c] for c in COLUMNS]}
        | {label: [values[col][i] for col in COLUMNS] for i, label in enumerate(cell_labels())}
    )


def render_period(subset, title):
    totals = subset[COLUMNS].sum()
    display(Markdown(
        f"**{int(totals['utterance_count']):,}** utterances · "
        f"**{int(totals['total_words']):,}** words"
    ))
    frame = summary_frame(subset)
    long = frame.melt(id_vars=["metric"], var_name="bucket", value_name="count")
    tok_plots.heatmap(long, x="bucket", y="metric", value="count", title=title)
    display(frame.set_index("metric"))
```

### Before 1920

```{python}
render_period(df[df.year < 1920], "Corpus composition before 1920")
```

### Full period (1900–1940)

```{python}
render_period(df, "Corpus composition 1900-1940")
```

### 1920 onwards

```{python}
render_period(df[df.year >= 1920], "Corpus composition from 1920")
```

## Data provenance

The two upstream sources are pinned by SHA-256 in
[`tok_preparer/src/download.py`](https://github.com/DigitalHistory-Lund/ToK-Preparer/blob/main/src/download.py).
The exact commits used to render this build are reported below.

```{python}
import subprocess
from pathlib import Path


def git_head(repo: Path) -> str:
    try:
        sha = subprocess.check_output(
            ["git", "-C", str(repo), "rev-parse", "HEAD"], text=True
        ).strip()
        desc = subprocess.check_output(
            ["git", "-C", str(repo), "log", "-1", "--format=%s"], text=True
        ).strip()
        return f"{sha[:12]} — {desc}"
    except Exception as exc:  # pragma: no cover
        return f"(unable to read: {exc})"


parent = Path().resolve()
submodule = parent / "tok_preparer"

print("Riksdagen speeches:  records_speeches v1.6.0")
print("                     sha256: a1c1310971214d4f836b72f48503b8d86bd3ec80763738e884a02e45a8f49ebf")
print("Riksdagen persons:   persons.sqlite   v1.2.2")
print("                     sha256: dfc0db29039715440b53d9820873c8c163fc72b5acdd207917e58bd4869ab5fd")
print()
print("ToK-explorer  parent HEAD:", git_head(parent))
print("tok_preparer  submodule HEAD:", git_head(submodule))
```
